name: IEC transparent D latch (rectangular form)
summary: IEC bistable with a static C1 control and 1D input; the output follows D while C1 is active.
description: The transparent latch is drawn like the D flip-flop but the C1 input has no dynamic wedge. While C1 is at its internal 1 state, the output follows the 1D input; when C1 returns to 0 the last value is held. TI's overview describes this as a level-operated control input.

Latches are used to capture data from a bus or to hold a value for a display or relay driver. In octal devices the common-control block carries C1 and the output enable, with eight per-bit elements below.

Because the output follows the input during the active level, glitches on D during that time pass through. The symbol shows this behaviour only through the absence of the wedge, so check it carefully.
readingNotes: No wedge on C1 means level-sensitive.
In octal parts, look for C1 in the common-control block.
drawingChecklist: Draw C1 without a dynamic mark.
Show output enable separately if present.
distinction: The IEC D flip-flop has a dynamic wedge on C1 and captures only at the edge.
